subject: Post-demo privacy recap — DPA & SCC module proposal for ClearVault
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Schultz <emma@clearvault.com>, ClearVault Security Team <security@clearvault.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo privacy recap — DPA & SCC module proposal for ClearVault

Hi Emma / team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate the clarity on your EU deployment needs. Short recap and proposed next steps on the privacy/security items you asked about:

1) SOC 2: we can provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report (2026) and a short executive summary. I’ve attached the report and put a copy in the Drive link below.

2) GDPR / DPA / SCC: you asked for the DPA and which SCC module we can sign. Our default stance for product usage is: Redwood Inference acts as a data processor on behalf of the customer (ClearVault) for customer-provided content. That means we offer a DPA that includes the processor-specific SCC module.

   Alternatives you asked about: if your legal team prefers a controller-to-controller framing for specific telemetry or aggregated metrics, we can discuss a narrow, scoped controller arrangement for those elements — but that will require legal review and a short statement of purpose / data mapping.

3) Technical / operational asks you raised: KMS integration for customer-managed keys (we support Bring Your Own Key via KMS/HSM integrations), retention & deletion controls (configurable project retention windows + deletion endpoints), and data location (EU region available).

Proposed next steps (timeline ~10 business days):
- I’ll send the DPA (processor version) for your counsel to review — signature via DocuSign if acceptable.
- Please fill the attached vendor security questionnaire (xlsx) and return to security@redwood.ai — helps us scope any additional controls.
- Grace (CC) from Legal & David from Ops will pick up any SOC2 evidence requests after we get the questionnaire back.

Attachments: redwood-dpa-summary.pdf, clearvault-security-questions.xlsx, SOC2-Redwood-2026-TypeII.pdf

If you’d like a short call with our legal/infosec to walk through the DPA/SCC choices, happy to coordinate.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0193

From: Emma Schultz <emma@clearvault.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01T17:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo privacy recap — DPA & SCC module proposal for ClearVault

Marcus — thanks for the summary and the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our legal and security side:

- We do need a DPA and prefer the SCC path rather than bespoke language. Our GC mentioned "processor module" is likely the right fit, but they also want to confirm whether Redwood is willing to accept a few controller obligations for aggregate telemetry (as you noted). That would be limited to telemetry used for service analytics and would not include PII or customer prompt data.

- On KMS: we will want to see the KMS architecture diagram and confirm that customer-managed keys can be scoped per-tenant.

- Retention: please include in the DPA the option to set a 30 / 90 / 365 day retention policy per project.

I’ve attached a preliminary security contact list and a short set of questions — we’ll fill the full questionnaire as Step 1 but wanted to surface these priorities.

Quick ask: Can you confirm whether Redwood will sign the standard EU SCC Module that treats Redwood as "processor" (not controller) for the main product? If so we can start legal review on our side.

Best,
Emma
Emma Schultz
Head of Legal Operations | ClearVault
emma@clearvault.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T09:03:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo privacy recap — DPA & SCC module proposal for ClearVault

Marcus — forwarding Emma's note. Quick internal take before we reply to ClearVault:

- Recommended position: accept signing the SCC variant that explicitly designates Redwood as Processor for customer content and metadata. This aligns with our standard DPA and avoids expanding controller-like obligations across the product surface.

- Telemetry exception: we can offer a narrow, contractual carve-out where Redwood collects aggregated, non-PII telemetry as a separate lawful-basis activity. For that, we should draft a one-paragraph "telemetry annex" and limit scope and retention.

- KMS & retention: Ops (David) should confirm the per-tenant KMS scoping and provide the architecture blurb Emma requested. Also prepare a template retention clause with selectable windows (30/90/365).

Action items:
- David: drop the KMS diagram and retention template into the Drive folder by EOD tomorrow.
- Marcus: send the processor DPA for signature and include a draft telemetry annex as an optional addendum.

If legal wants a short phone call with Emma’s team, I can join — I’ll keep the notes minimal and stick to contractual scope.

Thanks,
Grace
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Schultz <emma@clearvault.com>, ClearVault Security Team <security@clearvault.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-03T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo privacy recap — DPA & SCC module proposal for ClearVault

Emma — thanks for the quick reply and for flagging the items. Per internal alignment below, here’s a concrete plan and links so your team can start review:

1) DPA: I’ve initiated the processor DPA (Redwood as Processor) in DocuSign — link below. The DPA includes an optional telemetry annex (language attached as a separate PDF) that scopes only aggregated, non-PII metrics. If you want that annex removed, we can do that in the DocuSign flow.

DocuSign (DPA): https://app.docusign.com/embeddedSigning/abcdef123456
Drive (SOC2 + Evidence): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_dpa-soc2

2) Security questionnaire: attached is the XLSX we referenced. Please return the completed sheet to security@redwood.ai. Once we receive it, David will scope any additional evidence requests and provide the KMS architecture diagram.

3) Retention controls: the DPA includes a configurable retention clause with selectable windows (30 / 90 / 365 days) and an API-based deletion endpoint. We can record your preferred default in the DPA before signature.

Next steps for your side:
- Confirm whether you want the optional telemetry annex included.
- Complete and return the questionnaire (security@redwood.ai).
- Let us know preferred retention default so we can insert into the DPA before signing.

If your counsel wants a 30-minute alignment call, propose Wed 4/6 10:00-10:30 CET and I will loop in Grace and David.

Best,
Marcus
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0193
